newsitem.title: USA: NHL ice hockey - FLYERS BEAT RANGERS TO TAKE 1-0 LEAD.
newsitem.headline: NHL ice hockey - FLYERS BEAT RANGERS TO TAKE 1-0 LEAD.

text.p: The Philadelphia Flyers scored twice early in the first period and again in the third, and goalie Garth Snow came within 10 seconds of a shutout as the Flyers beat the New York Rangers 3-1 in the opening game of the Eastern Conference finals on Friday.
Rookies Dainius Zubrus and Janne Niinimaa scored 2:11 apart early in the first period and Eric Desjardins added a third-period goal to put the Flyers up 1-0 in the best-of-seven series.
Game two will be in Philadelphia on Sunday.
The Rangers did not score until Luc Robitaille lifted a backhander into the upper left corner of the net from the top of the crease with 10 seconds left in the game.

Snow, who finished with 24 saves, started the first nine games of the playoffs before Ron Hextall replaced him in the series-clinching victory over Buffalo in Game Six of the conference semifinals. Snow had played just 10 minutes in the playoffs prior to this year.
The Flyers have won each of their series openers this postseason and handed the Rangers their ninth straight series-opening loss, dating to the 1994 conference finals.
Zubrus, inserted onto the "Legion of Doom" line in place of right wing Mikael Renberg, gave the Flyers an early lead with his fifth postseason goal 2:28 into the game.

From the top of the left faceoff circle, LeClair unleashed a slap shot that was deflected into the slot. Zubrus grabbed the puck, headed for the net and swept a backhander past a sprawling Mike Richter.
The goal was reviewed and allowed to stand after replay showed Lindros was not in the crease.

Philadelphia won its seventh consecutive playoff game against the Rangers. The Flyers swept New York in the 1995 conference semifinals and won the final two games of the 1987 Patrick Division semifinals.
